answer.rationale: The 90-minute write-path latency degradation in the primary region began shortly after the release deployment, mirroring memory_b1 where rollback cleared a similar spike without customer impact. With settlement writes at peak, rollback directly targets the likely root cause (the release) while preserving write availability. Regional failover (memory_b2) would only mask a release-induced issue, and other options (add_capacity, circuit_breaker, read_replicas) fail to address write-path latency. Staged release practices (memory_b6) support the hypothesis of a canary deployment, making rollback safe and effective.
